docs.title: Verboisy
docs.text:
Verboisy combines model-directed browser navigation, schema validation and durable SQLite records. The CLI and Python API share one implementation.

Install the checked-out source (a published package is not assumed):

python -m pip install -e .
python -m playwright install chromium
verboisy run --help

Configure a LiteLLM model and its credentials before a live run. System dependencies may be required for Chromium. Linux installations can use python -m playwright install --with-deps chromium with appropriate system privileges.

The release audit, exact reproduction steps, requirement matrix, and verification limits are in the delivered engineering report. Browser and live-model acceptance must be checked separately from offline test coverage.

  • API
  • Authentic demo and live acceptance
  • Validation and release

docs.title: Python and command-line API
docs.text:
from verboisy import RunResult, run

result: RunResult = run(
    goal="Open https://ycombinator.com/companies and find AI companies in the F26 batch",
    schema="examples/yc_startups/schema.json",
    export="result.json",
)
print(result.run_id, result.completed, result.records)

The schema may be a string path, a Path, or a dictionary. New runs require a nonblank goal and schema. Resume with run(resume=True) or run(resume="saved-id"). A saved goal/schema takes precedence over supplied replacements. An export destination can be overridden. A completed id can be re-exported without opening a browser.

run and arun accept keyword-only goal, schema, export, resume, headless, max_steps, and optional config: Settings. Use await arun(...) inside an existing event loop. headless=None uses environment configuration. Step, timeout and request budgets renew per invocation.

RunResult field Meaning run_id Stable full id; a unique prefix is accepted for resume records Every saved record, including any preserved legacy duplicates export_path Absolute path actually written, or None db_path Absolute database path completed True only after FINISH and successful collection validation status COMPLETED or PAUSED for normal returns stop_reason planner_finished, max_steps, model_budget or run_timeout

Errors raise VerboisyError (or configuration validation errors); async cancellation propagates after cleanup. Durable saved rows remain available. The command line uses exit 0 for completion, 1 for errors, 2 for incomplete budgets or argument syntax, and 130 for Ctrl-C.

verboisy run --goal "Read a public directory" --schema examples/yc_startups/schema.json
verboisy run --resume
verboisy run --resume saved-id --export result.csv
verboisy run --help

Resume restores the last saved URL, not a complete browser session. JSON Schema validates data shape, not factual truth. See the README for configuration and limitations.

docs.title: Authentic demonstration and live acceptance
docs.text:
The supplied .cast and docs/demo.gif are illustrative historical material. They are not evidence of a successful run. The original recording shows 13 saved rows, interruption, resume and a final 40-row export; the supplied source had no resume implementation and could not produce that workflow. Do not publish it as a current verified demonstration.

The fixture below uses a real browser, real configured model, actual validation and SQLite persistence. It does not fabricate planner output, records, or progress logs. The HTTP endpoint used in automated tests is explicitly a model stub; do not use that test as an autonomous-product demo.

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
From the repository root, complete installation and run the validation commands in validation.md. Configure .env with the real model credentials, or a running local Ollama endpoint. API calls can incur provider charges.

poetry run python scripts/live_demo.py

The script serves the supplied two-card directory on an ephemeral loopback port, uses a fresh uniquely named run directory under demo-runs, pauses after a bounded number of actions, resumes any incomplete run, and verifies the actual output against the fixture values. ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK is enabled only in those child processes to allow the local page. Chromium sandboxing remains enabled unless the operator has explicitly configured otherwise. A failing or incomplete run returns nonzero.

For the actual public YC workflow, from the repository root:

poetry run verboisy run \
  --goal "Open https://www.ycombinator.com/companies and find AI startups in the Fall 2026 batch. Use page evidence for batch and category." \
  --schema examples/yc_startups/schema.json \
  --export result.json

Check the source pages yourself. Record count, batch availability, and model behavior depend on the live site. No fixed count of 40 is promised.

To verify Ctrl-C recovery, use a fresh database and goal, wait for an actual SAVE log, press Ctrl-C once, then run verboisy run --resume using the same SQLITE_DB_PATH. Check that the recorded run id is unchanged and saved records persist without new duplicates. A second interrupt during shutdown or an uncommitted current operation cannot be promised lossless.

docs.title: Record the real terminal
docs.text:
Install asciinema and the agg converter using their official installation guides. Record only an environment with no visible secrets:

asciinema rec docs/demo.cast
poetry run python scripts/live_demo.py
exit
agg docs/demo.cast docs/demo.gif

These lines are sequential interactive steps: the middle command runs inside the recording shell, and exit closes that shell. Replay the cast and compare its logs, run id, actual SQLite rows and export before replacing the README's historical-demo notice with the new GIF. Retain the generated evidence directory alongside the cast. Do not edit console output to invent records or hide a failed acceptance check.

A replacement live recording was not produced in the audit environment: no provider credentials were supplied, and Chromium downloads failed there.

docs.title: Validation and release workflow
docs.text:
Execute these commands from the repository root after installing Poetry 2.5.1 and Python 3.11 or later. The supplied .python-version selects 3.11.9; the audit used that version. CI also covers newer Python minors, whose results must be checked in CI.

poetry install
poetry check --lock
poetry run ruff check .
poetry run ruff format --check .
poetry run mypy src
poetry run pytest -m "not browser" --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing
poetry run pip-audit --local
poetry run mkdocs build --strict
poetry build

Success means zero exit status. Coverage must meet the existing 80% threshold. The audit's offline tests replace browser/model decisions where stated; they do not establish real model accuracy. The local HTTP test uses the actual LiteLLM transport with a stub model response.

Required Chromium gate on Linux/macOS:

poetry run playwright install --with-deps chromium
VERBOISY_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1 poetry run pytest -m browser -v

PowerShell equivalent for the second command:

$env:VERBOISY_REQUIRE_BROWSER = "1"
poetry run pytest -m browser -v
Remove-Item Env:VERBOISY_REQUIRE_BROWSER

The browser fixture uses a local HTTP server and explicitly disables Chromium's OS sandbox inside the test process only. Product defaults remain sandboxed. Test the default sandbox separately on the intended deployment OS/container.

If installation fails, resolve the interpreter/package error before proceeding. If Chromium cannot download or launch, the browser gate is blocked, not passed. If pip-audit cannot reach the advisory service, no clean-security claim follows. If a test fails, retain the traceback and database; do not relax assertions or mark the run completed merely to produce an export.

Run live acceptance with the intended model/provider after these checks. Build/install the wheel in a fresh virtual environment and test python -m verboisy --help and the documented source examples.

The publication workflow repeats tests/build on the release tag and checks that v<version> matches pyproject.toml. Configure trusted publishing with PyPI and the protected pypi GitHub environment before publishing. No release was published as part of the audit. A green local suite is not a substitute for a green release workflow, live acceptance, and deployment-specific checks.
